concepts.description: Generation preserves separation of concerns, dependency inversion, single responsibility, open-closed, and interface-segregation principles.
The base command interactively selects project metadata, frontend, backend, database, authentication, features, and deployment.
Quick initialization defaults to Next.js with TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL with Prisma, JWT, Jest, and Playwright.
React, Vue, Next.js, Nuxt, Angular, and SvelteKit retain their documented routing, state, styling, form, API, authentication, and test integrations.
Express, Fastify, NestJS, FastAPI, Django, Gin, Fiber, and Actix retain their documented validation, authentication, ORM, database, cache, logging, documentation, and test integrations.
Supported database choices are exactly PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB, constrained by the selected backend framework.
Frontend generation controls TypeScript, styling, state management, and test framework; TypeScript is enabled by default.
Components can select paths, tests, and stories; pages can select layouts, protection, and matching API routes.
Backend generation controls database, ORM, authentication strategy, and Docker inclusion.
Modules can add CRUD, events, or queue workers; endpoints can select methods, authentication, and validation.
Models can define fields, relations, timestamps, and soft deletion.
Fresh migration drops every table before rerunning migrations.
Testing supports setup plus unit, integration, and end-to-end additions with coverage and watch options.
DevOps generation produces per-service Docker files, local and production Compose files, CI for four platforms, and deployment configuration for six targets.
The configuration file retains project metadata, version, author, license, selected package managers, and stack versions.
Frontend configuration retains UI, dark mode, persisted state, app routing, middleware, i18n locales, forms, API retry and cache, testing, and build controls.
Backend configuration retains clean modules, REST versioning and prefix, documentation path, transformed whitelisted validation, and local or OAuth providers.
Database pooling, migrations, Redis cache, queues, rotating logs, CORS, rate limits, CSRF, and unit, integration, and end-to-end tests remain configured.

User, refresh-token, post, product, order, order-item, and category models retain fields, relations, indexes, uniqueness, optionals, defaults, roles, order states, decimal precision, and refresh-token storage.
Develop auto-deploys to staging, while main-to-production disables auto deployment and requires approval.
AWS deployment retains its region and frontend, backend, database, and cache service mapping plus error-rate and latency alerts.
Development values are placeholders; staging and production database, Redis, and JWT secrets come from environment secret management.
Initialization creates the root workspace, Git state, package files, environment examples, and secret-management setup.
Frontend generation configures framework, TypeScript, UI, state, routing guards, API integration, and test examples.
Backend generation configures framework, persistence, authentication, layered modules, validation, API documentation, and tests.
Integration generates shared API types, validates contracts, connects URLs, proxy, and CORS, and wires refresh and protected routes.
DevOps generation creates multi-stage containers, CI, optional Terraform, cloud resources, and monitoring.
Documentation generation creates README, contribution, API, authentication, error, deployment, architecture, style, PR, and testing guidance.
Frontend and backend trees separate application, components, hooks, stores, utilities, modules, common infrastructure, configuration, database code, and tests, joined by shared API types.
Generated artifacts cover configuration, source languages, Prisma schemas and migrations, documentation, environment files, containers, OpenAPI and HTML docs, scripts, and optional Terraform.
Generated APIs validate and whitelist requests and apply Helmet, CORS, CSP, CSRF, and rate limiting.
New and updated passwords use bcrypt cost 10, password fields are excluded from responses, users update only themselves unless admin, and create or delete routes are admin guarded.
Missing users and bad passwords share the same invalid-credentials response; duplicate registration, successful registration, login, and invalid credentials retain their respective HTTP statuses.
Access and refresh tokens use separate secrets and TTLs; refresh tokens are stored with expiry, rotated on refresh, deleted on logout, and expiration seconds are converted to milliseconds.
Missing or expired stored refresh tokens are rejected as unauthorized.

API types, CORS, refresh handling, protected routes, validation, documentation, dependency injection, strict TypeScript, accessibility, i18n, and tests are generated behavior rather than advisory prose.
Reference CI uses the documented Node, pnpm, PostgreSQL, and Redis versions, database ports, health timings, retries, coverage target, job dependencies, and production branch gate.
The sample button and pagination retain their focus-ring, opacity, hover, height, page, and limit constants as examples rather than universal policy.
The container uses frozen dependency installation, dependency and builder copy stages, port exposure, and PostgreSQL health-check controls.
SaaS, shop, and blog recipes retain their respective frontend, backend, database, authentication, and feature selections.
Database recovery checks service state and the connection string before pushing the schema.
Authentication recovery checks both JWT secrets and regenerates a 64-byte random secret.
Build recovery removes only the listed local dependency and build caches, then reinstalls and rebuilds in the intended project.
Next.js, NestJS, Prisma, and Tailwind documentation retain their canonical URLs.
